reporting-org.narrative: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights

title.narrative: Protection and Promotion of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms for refugees and host communities

description.narrative: To enhance the protection, promotion, and realization of human rights and fundamental freedom of the refugees and host communities in Kenya

participating-org.narrative: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights

title.narrative: Duty bearers and stakeholders (CUC, Committee & working group members) trained on HRBA application to refugees and host communities

description.narrative: Targeted capacity building of key duty bearers involved in refugee management is critical in the overall enjoyment and upholding the rights of refugees. This grant supports training of police officers, judicial officers and refugee technical working groups

title.narrative: Number of duty key bearers trained on HRBA application to refugees and host communities’ matters

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of duty key bearers who have received training on applying a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) to matters concerning refugees and host communities. It also tracks the quantity of duty key bearers, such Law Enforcement Agents , CUC members , Refugee Committee members and Working groups who have undergone training specifically focused on integrating human rights principles into their work with refugees and host communities

comment.narrative: The capacity of 270 law enforcement officers was enhanced on refugee rights, refugee approved documentations and the application of Human Rights Based Approach in discharging their duties especially when handling refugee matters. Additionally, A total of 15 CUC trainings were conducted in Garissa, Dadaab, Nairobi, Mombasa, Lodwar, Eldoret and Kakuma reaching 591 stakeholders mainly police officers, immigration officials, prison officers, civil society organisations and justice actors. These trainings focused capacity strengthening of participants on the Refugee Act 2021, human rights-based approach, counselling skills, and offered guidance on psychological first aid, stress management and raised awareness on the complexities of forced migration

title.narrative: Victims of human rights violations provided with appropriate redress and resolution of complaints

description.narrative: The KNCHR in line with its statutory and constitutional mandate receive and process complaints on alleged human rights violations. Complaints that fall within the KNCHR’s mandate are subjected to further analysis and follow up that includes among others investigations. Complaints that fall outside the KNCHR’s mandate are referred to relevant complaints handling institutions for further action.

title.narrative: Number of cases resolved through Alternative Dispute Resolution

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of cases resolved through Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), specifically within the recommended time frame set by the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) and the Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK). It tracks the quantity of cases successfully resolved through non-adversarial methods, such as mediation or negotiation, promoting timely and efficient resolution of human rights disputes outside of formal court processes.

comment.narrative: The KNCHR successfully mediated between 2 cases; 1) Between a refugee and security officer and 2) Between refugees and a hospital. In the first case, the Kakuma based refugee had complained of assault and threats from camp security officer within the camp. The accused officer was redeployed to another station and the refugees relocated to a safer location within the camp. For the second case, 5 south sudanese refugees had been detained at a hospital due to medical bill arrears. The KNCHR facilitated mediation between the refugees and the hospital management where an amicable arrangement for settlement of the bill was agreed upon by both parties. These two cases touched on Civil and political rights and group rights.

title.narrative: Number of Cases received and processed

description.narrative: The total number of human rights complaints received, processed and documented by the KNCHR

comment.narrative: During the reporting period a total of 1,082 complaints were received and processed as per the entries in the Complaint management systems as at the end of the first year of the project. Violations on Economic Social and Cultural (ECOSOC) rights formed the highest number of complaints received accounting for 454(42%) followed by Civil political rights 408 (38%) and Group rights 220 (20%). Among the received cases, 131 complaints translating to 12% were received from refugees, 951 complaints were received from the host communities. Out of the 1.082 cases received, 645 were given legal advice,435 were admitted for investigations and further processing and 2 complaints were in the pending state awaiting decision whether to admit or provide legal advice

title.narrative: Number of PILs undertaken to affirm human rights

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of Public Interest Litigations (PILs) undertaken to affirm human rights. It tracks the quantity of legal cases filed on behalf of the public or marginalized groups to protect and assert human rights. The indicator reflects the level of legal advocacy and litigation efforts aimed at advancing human rights principles and addressing violations through judicial means.

comment.narrative: A total of 6 PILs were undertaken. Through the KNCHR intervention of conducting trial observations before Kitale Law Courts in R vs. Hussein Ibrahim MCSO E097 of 2023, the victim’s right to access justice was upheld. The accused person was alleged to have defiled the Congolese Refugee minor sometime in June 2023 along the railway line close to ASK showground Kitale where the refugees sought refuge. Through intervention by the project team the accused person was found guilty of defilement contrary to section 8(1) as read with section 8(3) of the Sexual Offences Act No. 3 of 2006 as read with Section 215 of the Criminal Procedure Code and sentenced to 10 years imprisonment and the judgment was delivered on 21st December 2023. The remaining 5 cases are ongoing and the KNCHR is actively watching briefs pending judgement

title.narrative: Refugees and host communities trained and sensitized on rights and fundamental freedoms and participate in decision making processes and peacebuilding

description.narrative: The grants supports a rights awareness program through trainings and community forums of rights holders (Refugees and Host communities) on rights awareness including enhancing their ability to claim their rights. This intervention aims to lead to their increased understanding of human rights, their duties and responsibilities, the refugee act 2021, importance of integration as well as the mandates of different institutions managing their affairs in the country.

title.narrative: Number of refugees & Host Communities trained on human rights, refugee law and peace building

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of refugees & Host Communities trained on human rights, refugee law and peace building.

comment.narrative: The project built the capacity building of 686 rights holders (Refugees and Host communities) on rights awareness, HRBA, Refugee Act 2021 and enhancing their ability to claim their rights. The TOTs created a pool of trainers who cascaded the knowledge acquired from training sessions to participants during community dialogue forums

title.narrative: Number of refugees and host communities sensitized on their rights and freedoms, social governance and peacebuilding issues

description.narrative: This indicator documents the total number of refugee and host communities members sensitized on Human rights through awareness forums and celebration of human rights thematic days

comment.narrative: The KNCHR reached 5484 refugees and host community members through targeted community forums across all project implementation sites, social media advocacy campaigns, and celebration of human rights thematic awareness days such as International Human Rights Day 2023, and World Refugee Day 2024. The participants also appreciated the need for peaceful co-existence between the refugees and host community

title.narrative: Refugees & host communities accessing mental health and psychosocial support services

description.narrative: Through this output, the project will contribute to the well-being and resilience of refugees, host communities and duty bearers especially police officers in Kenya, by addressing the mental health and psychosocial consequences of displacement and providing legal assistance. The refugees and host communities will have increased access to legal aid and quality MHPSS services, which will be delivered through community-based approaches that are sensitive to cultural and gender-specific needs.

title.narrative: Number of refugees and the host communities. sensitized on mental health and trauma management

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of refugees and host communities who have undergone sensitization programs focused on mental health and trauma management. It tracks the quantity of individuals who receive targeted awareness and education sessions to enhance their understanding of mental health issues, trauma, and strategies for coping and recovery.

comment.narrative: The project team in Dadaab, Nairobi and Kakuma conducted 6 community dialogue forums on mental health and conflict resolution, drug abuse, prevention and response to violence against women and girls reaching 153 participants who included members of majority and minority community groups, PWDs, elderly, youth, women and Community Health Volunteers.

title.narrative: Number of police officers who attended the debriefing sessions

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of police officers reached through debriefing sessions

comment.narrative: The project team in Dadaab, Nairobi and Kakuma conducted 5 psychoeducation forums for police officers reaching 106 duty bearers. Notably, most of the participants in Dadaab were new transfers who had not been previously trained on refugee and host community protection, and who reported to have gained in depth knowledge on these subjects after the training. The forums also focused on suicide prevention, healthy coping strategies and selfcare, vicarious trauma and utilizing PFA in crisis interventions

title.narrative: Number of refugees & host communities that have access to adequate mental health and psychosocial support

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of refugees and host communities who have access to sufficient mental health and psychosocial support services. It will track the quantity of individuals who receive appropriate assistance, counseling, and resources to address their mental health needs and promote their psychosocial well-being.

comment.narrative: The project team in Kakuma, Dadaab, and Garissa provided psychosocial services reaching 401 FDSPs while Nairobi conducted group therapy sessions (3 Groups for 4 sessions for 10 individuals) totalling 120 clients,4 families and couple therapy session for a family of 4 members contributing to a stronger reception of our message and enhanced our advocacy against the unlawful use of Alternative Justice Systems (AJS), particularly in SGBV cases.
